practices.name: Session->account affinity with TTL
practices.does: Bind a session to one upstream credential and reuse it until TTL expires or the credential becomes unavailable; write the binding on success, drop it on failure.
practices.why: Caches are per org/workspace (D-openai-pc: 'Caches are not shared across organizations'; D-ant-pc: workspace isolation), so every account switch forfeits the cache. About 90% of our input is cache reads, which makes this the dominant cost lever. The TTL should cover the upstream cache life: OpenAI GPT-5.6+ at least 30 min; Anthropic 5 min or 1 h.
practices.metric: account switches per session; cache_read_tokens/input_tokens per session; cache-miss rate on the first request after a switch

practices.name: Session-key extraction precedence
practices.does: Take explicit client session headers first, then prompt_cache_key or conversation id, then a derived hash. Scope the key by caller identity so two callers cannot steer each other.
impl: cpa selector.go:1587-1602 (12-step order: X-Claude-Code-Session-Id ... Session-Id ... prompt_cache_key ... first-message hash)
bifrost core/schemas/useragents.go:84-92 (x-claude-code-session-id, x-session-affinity, x-session-id, session-id, session_id, thread-id, conversation_id)
newapi channel_affinity_setting.go:125-134 (Codex: body prompt_cache_key on /v1/responses),140-149 (Claude: metadata.user_id)
litellm deployment_affinity_check.py:249-255 (key scoped by hashed user key)
codex codex-api/src/requests/headers.rs:5-14 (session-id, thread-id); endpoint/responses.rs:88 (x-client-request-id); core/src/client.rs:571-592 (prompt_cache_key = session id)
practices.metric: share of requests resolved from an explicit key rather than the hash fallback; cross-caller key collisions (target 0)

practices.name: Pass cache keys through unchanged; affinity key includes the cache partition
practices.does: Never rewrite prompt_cache_key or session headers. Include partition fields in the routing key so the router never claims a hit the upstream cannot serve.
impl: D-openai-pc model table: GPT-5.6+ prompt_cache_key is 'Optional for separate cache accounting'; earlier models use it for routing, at about 15 rpm per key
practices.why: Treating GPT-6 as 'GPT-5.6 and later' is my inference; the doc covers API orgs, not the ChatGPT subscription backend.
practices.metric: outbound prompt_cache_key == inbound (target 100%)

practices.name: Prefix/prompt-cache-aware placement
practices.does: Route to the credential or replica that already served the prefix, including forks and compactions that carry no session key.
impl: litellm prompt_caching_deployment_check.py:4,50-120 (records model_id per cacheable prefix on success)
practices.why: For hosted upstreams the cache owner is the account, and the upstream routes machines itself. Engine KV routers (smg, llm-d, dynamo, prodstack) apply only to locally served models, such as the memory services. The LCP matcher helps requests with no session key.
practices.metric: cache-hit ratio on requests with no session key

practices.name: Stateful-continuation pinning (encrypted reasoning, previous_response_id)
practices.does: Send a request that carries replayed encrypted reasoning or a previous_response_id to the account that minted it. While that account is cooled down, fail fast with 429 + Retry-After instead of re-routing.
impl: codex core/src/client.rs:955 (include reasoning.encrypted_content),993 (store:false) -- always sent at this pin
litellm encrypted_content_affinity_check.py:1-13,374-400 (fail fast with Retry-After); deployment_affinity_check.py:441-455 (previous_response_id has highest priority)
bifrost core/encryptedreasoning.go:120-136 (content is bound to the minting identity)
practices.quality_risk: The strip fallbacks are lossy: litellm encrypted_content_affinity_check.py:351 and bifrost encryptedreasoning.go:220 stripUnverifiableReasoning. They are forbidden without a passed quality gate.
practices.metric: invalid_encrypted_content 400s (target 0); strip events (target 0); fail-fast 429s while the origin is cooled

practices.name: Subagent/fork credential inheritance
practices.does: Child sessions reuse the parent's credential.
impl: bifrost core/schemas/useragents.go:81-83 (deliberately omits parent-session headers so sub-agents are not collapsed onto the parent key)
codex client.rs:571-592 (internal sessions use cache key {source}:{parent_thread_id}; non-root agents send their own session id)
practices.why: The trade-off is cache reuse against spreading quota.
practices.metric: subagent cache_read share vs per-account window-utilization spread

practices.name: Bounded stickiness (break threshold)
practices.does: Keep affinity until a load, latency or availability penalty exceeds a threshold.
impl: cpa selector.go:965-969 (an established binding outranks priority; rebind only on unavailability)
practices.why: Our break trigger should be quota or availability, not latency. Breaking costs a cache re-write (1.25x on GPT-5.6+ per D-openai-pc) and conflicts with P5.
practices.quality_risk: none for plain sessions; see P5 for reasoning sessions
practices.metric: rebinding rate; p95 latency sticky vs non-sticky

practices.name: Quota-aware credential selection from passive headers
practices.does: Use upstream window headers to choose cold bindings and to avoid accounts that are near their limit.
impl: cpa sdk/cliproxy/auth/quota_signals.go:26-36,149-163 (captures retry-after, anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*, x-codex-*; observation only, does not drive scheduling)
aigw site/docs/capabilities/traffic/quota-policy.md:9-10,36 (token budgets; 429 when all buckets are exceeded)
practices.evidence: source-reviewed (header semantics are client-source only; server semantics not verified)
practices.why: Subscription windows are the binding constraint. None of the reviewed upstreams drives selection from x-codex-* headers (cpa only observes them), so this wiring has no reference implementation.
practices.metric: 429 rate per account; spread of window utilization across accounts

practices.name: Per-account 429 cooldown honoring Retry-After/reset
practices.does: Cool down only the failing credential, for the upstream-stated duration.
impl: litellm router.py:8301-8320 (priority: deployment config > response header > default); constants.py:75 (default 5 s); cooldown_handlers.py:387 (a 429 cools only when alternatives exist)
cpa config.example.yaml:179-190 (transient 5xx cooldown, 60 s legacy default, separate from quota)
portkey src/globals.ts:7-11; handlers/retryHandler.ts:122 (retry-after-ms, x-ms-retry-after-ms, retry-after; 60 s cap)
D-cc-gw: return retry-after as integer seconds; a value above 60 stops Claude Code's retries
practices.metric: requests sent to a cooled account (target 0); 429s immediately after cooldown expiry

practices.name: Same-model credential failover
practices.does: On a retryable failure, re-pick another credential for the same model and effort. Never fall back to another model.
impl: litellm router.py:804 (enable_weighted_failover: re-pick within the group before cross-group fallback)
cpa config.example.yaml:153-177 (request-retry rounds across credentials on 403/408/429/5xx)
bifrost core/sessionaffinity.go:99-102 (a binding names provider+model; never follows a provider onto an older model)
D-or-pr (allow_fallbacks across providers of the same model)
practices.why: Applies to cold sessions and to requests without replayed reasoning. For bound reasoning sessions, P5 fail-fast wins.
practices.quality_risk: Cross-model fallback is a downgrade: litellm cross-group fallbacks, cpa legacy switch-preview-model.
practices.metric: failover success rate; requested-model != served-model count (target 0)

practices.name: Circuit breaker / outlier ejection per account
practices.does: Eject a credential after consecutive or rate-based failures, with half-open recovery. Keep auth-dead (401), quota (429) and transient (5xx) failures separate.
impl: smg model_gateway/src/config/types.rs:1098-1114 (failure 10, success 3, open 60 s, window 120 s)
litellm cooldown_handlers.py:318-395 (failure-rate cooldown with a minimum-request threshold)
D-or-pr (deprioritize providers with outages in the last 30 s)
practices.metric: time to eject; false-ejection rate

practices.name: Retry budget, exponential backoff with jitter, one retry owner
practices.does: Cap retries per request and per client, and retry at exactly one layer.
impl: smg crates/external_router/src/retry_config.rs:8-28 (5 retries, 50 ms->30 s, x1.5, jitter 0.2); retry.rs:10-20 (408/429/500/502/503/504)
D-sre ch.21 (per-request budget of 3 attempts; per-client retry ratio below 10%; retry only at the layer immediately above)
practices.why: The clients (Codex, Claude Code, the SDKs) already retry, so gateway retries multiply on top of theirs.
practices.metric: retries/requests (target 10% or less); upstream attempts per client request

practices.name: Request hedging
practices.does: Race a duplicate request after the per-try timeout.
practices.why: It doubles subscription quota, the duplicate lands without a warm cache, and output is non-deterministic.
practices.metric: n/a

practices.name: Idempotency/dedup
practices.does: Collapse duplicate requests by Idempotency-Key.
practices.why: Generation is non-deterministic and the official SDKs send no idempotency key. The practice that actually applies is P21.
practices.metric: n/a

practices.name: Semantic/model routing
practices.does: Classify the request and choose a model or tier.
impl: D-or-pc (auto router may select a different model on a later turn)
practices.why: It can downgrade model or effort, which violates the hard constraint. The only exception is a candidate set of identical model+effort targets.
practices.metric: n/a

practices.name: Routing-decision observability
practices.does: Keep one correlation id end to end, and emit served-by credential, routing reason, attempt count and cache usage on every request.
practices.metric: share of requests with the same correlation id at every hop; served-by, reason and attempts present (target 100%)

practices.name: Multi-instance chaining
practices.does: Exactly one hop owns account selection, affinity and retries. Other hops forward session, cache and sticky headers byte for byte, propagate deadlines (inner timeout below outer) and keep the trace id.
impl: cpa internal/home/{requests.go}:15; client.go:1318-1323 (retry_round propagated to the remote node)
litellm deployment_affinity_check.py:63-73 (Redis claim-pin, first writer wins across instances)
practices.quality_risk: see P22 for the compression hop
practices.metric: upstream attempts per client request across both hops; hops making affinity decisions (target 1)

practices.name: Per-credential concurrency cap
practices.does: Admission control for in-flight requests per credential, with a typed busy error plus Retry-After.
practices.why: Unknown whether the ChatGPT or Claude subscriptions enforce per-account concurrency.
practices.metric: concurrent streams per account; 429s correlated with concurrency

practices.name: Upstream sticky-token round trip
practices.does: Pass x-codex-turn-state through unchanged in both directions, and keep one account for the whole turn.
impl: codex core/src/client.rs:13,159,278-283 (a sticky-routing token that must be replayed for all requests within the turn),585 ('ChatGPT derives cache affinity from the Responses session-id header')
practices.metric: turns with a turn-state mismatch or an account change (target 0)

practices.name: Claude Code gateway contract
practices.does: Forward anthropic-beta, anthropic-version and the system array unchanged, with the attribution block kept first. Return retry-after as integer seconds. Pass x-should-retry, anthropic-ratelimit-unified-* and error bodies through unchanged.
practices.quality_risk: Reshaping the system array changes the prompt-cache key and defeats the attribution strip.
practices.metric: contract header pass-through rate (target 100%)

practices.name: Stream-safe retry
practices.does: Never retry or fall back after the first content chunk reaches the client.
impl: D-envoy (hedging and retry apply before the response is returned)
practices.quality_risk: Violating it splices two generations into one response.
practices.metric: duplicated or spliced streams (target 0)

practices.name: Prefix byte-stability
practices.does: The gateway never mutates any byte of the cached prefix: tools, then system/instructions, then earlier messages.
impl: D-ant-pc 'What invalidates the cache' (100% identical segments required; tools, system and thinking changes invalidate everything downstream)
codex core/src/client.rs:330-385 (incremental reuse only when all request properties match)
practices.why: This applies directly to the 20129 full-compression hop. Rewriting earlier turns invalidates the cache from the edit point and is a lossy rewrite.
practices.quality_risk: HIGH unless the compression passes a quality gate
practices.metric: per-session cache_read/input_tokens with vs without the 20129 hop on identical traffic

addendum_2026_09_28.P1_P7_clarification: Reviewed upstreams never let a post-affinity step move a bound session (cpa selector.go:965-969; litellm deployment_affinity_check.py:473-500; bifrost core/sessionaffinity.go:45-48). P7 break conditions are explicit bounds (llm-d MaxTTFTPenaltyMs plugin.go:75-78; smg cache_aware.rs:98-101, prefix_hash.rs:16-19; smg manual.rs:3-8 remaps only when unhealthy). Occupancy belongs in P18 admission control on the pinned credential (cpa home_concurrency.go:23-29,326).
addendum_2026_09_28.live_finding_20128_WITHDRAWN: route-mapper: over 24 h, 8.4% of pinned GPT-6 turns on 20128 were served by a different account because of a post-affinity OAuth occupancy step. Cache-read share on those turns was 84.1% vs 93.9%.
addendum_2026_09_28.live_finding_20128_recomputed: route-mapper recomputed after finding call_logs.timestamp is the request END time. Over the last 24h on 20128, 201 Codex conversations with a unique pin match had 4,461 turns. 460 of them (10.3%, in 64 conversations) were served off-pin. All 460 had served priority <= pinned priority + 1, where a uniform null predicts 0.77. The occupancy condition held on 334 of the 460 overrides, against 166 of the 4,001 on-pin turns. Cache-read share was 73.8% off-pin vs 92.1% on-pin, about 5.4M extra uncached input tokens per 24h. route-mapper's claim, unverified by route-landscape: upstream PR #8940 meant affinity to outrank occupancy, but auth.ts:2159-2177 applies the override after the pin, so this is an ordering defect. P19 and P5 checks pending.
